answers_by_date.answer: Equal access to all types of social security protections after some period of time
answers_by_date.basis: Contributory pensions under DL 3.500 (1980), art. 2: every dependent worker is affiliated automatically, with no nationality test. Ley 18.156 (as amended by Ley 18.726, 1988) only let foreign technicians who kept a foreign scheme opt out and later get a refund. The non-contributory assistance pension (PASIS, DL 869/1975) required 3 years' continuous residence. No practice evidence specific to this period was found; the rating is carried over from the starting answer.

answers_by_date.answer: Equal access to all types of social security protections after some period of time
answers_by_date.basis: Same framework as in 2000: DL 3.500 art. 2, the Ley 18.156 opt-out and the PASIS 3-year residence condition. No practice evidence for this period; the rating is carried over.

answers_by_date.answer: Equal access to all types of social security protections after some period of time
answers_by_date.basis: Ley 20.255 (pension reform; Pensión Básica Solidaria in force from July 2008) replaced PASIS with the basic solidarity pension. Its art. 3(c) requires 20 years' residence, including 4 of the last 5 years. The waiting period got longer but stayed within the same answer option; contributory affiliation did not change. Superintendencia de Pensiones data show 18,590 new foreign affiliates in 2009, so foreign workers were in practice being affiliated.

answers_by_date.answer: Equal access to all types of social security protections after some period of time
answers_by_date.basis: No change to DL 3.500 art. 2, Ley 18.156 or Ley 20.255 art. 3. The Superintendencia study (reported by Emol, Jan 2020) shows foreign affiliation rising steeply between 2009 and 2018. It also notes a 13–14-month delay in obtaining a RUN (national ID number), during which workers contribute under a provisional ID. Ley 21.325 art. 16 (2022) came later.

answers.change_2000_2020: There have been right protections both in 2000 and 2020 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

events.what_changed: Repealed letter a) of art. 1 and added art. 7, which lets foreign workers with AFP contributions claim a refund if they meet the art. 1 conditions. This is an optional exemption for foreign technicians, not a denial of coverage. It predates 2000 and was in force throughout.
events.passage: Artículo 7°.- En el caso de que trabajadores extranjeros registraren cotizaciones en una Administradora de Fondos de Pensiones, podrán solicitar la devolución de los fondos previsionales que hubieren depositado, siempre que den cumplimiento a los requisitos establecidos en el artículo 1° de esta ley.

events.what_changed: Created the Pensión Básica Solidaria de vejez, replacing PASIS (DL 869, which required 3 years' continuous residence; read via SUSESO Dictamen 10744-1985). The new pension requires 20 years' residence, including 4 of the last 5. The residence-period condition remains, so the answer option is unchanged.
events.passage: c) Acreditar residencia en el territorio de la República de Chile por un lapso no inferior a veinte años continuos o discontinuos, contados desde que el peticionario haya cumplido veinte años de edad; y, en todo caso, por un lapso no inferior a cuatro años de residencia en los últimos cinco años

events.what_changed: Administrative interpretation confirming that PASIS required 3 years' continuous residence immediately before the application. This was the rule in force in 2000 and 2005.
events.passage: podrán gozar de pensión asistencial las personas inválidas mayores de 18 años y los ancianos mayores de 65 años que carecen de recursos y que tengan una residencia continua en el país, de por lo menos, tres años inmediatamente anteriores a la fecha de la presentación de la solicitud

events.what_changed: Labour Directorate ruling: foreign workers must pay unemployment-insurance contributions even when exempt from pension contributions under Ley 18.156. The Directorate also enforces contribution duties for foreign workers who lack a work visa.

answers.sourcing_note: I could not read the full LeyChile texts and version histories (the API needs a key and long laws load only their index), so the texts came from SUSESO, Superintendencia de Pensiones and iura copies. sources_opened.title: Superintendencia de Pensiones Título XI Ley 18.156
Superintendencia de Pensiones – Los migrantes y el sistema de pensiones

answers.starting_answer_concern: The 2020 answer cannot rest on Ley 21.325 art. 16 (in force 2022). It rests on DL 3.500 art. 2 (immediate, nationality-neutral contributory coverage) and Ley 20.255 art. 3 (20-year residence for the non-contributory pension), which together support the same option. 'Effectively Always' is generous: the Superintendencia study documents 13–14-month RUN delays and provisional-ID contributions, and informal work keeps many migrants out of coverage. 'Usually' would be more consistent with the MRD's guidance.
answers.notes: Between 2000 and 2020 the only substantive change was the 2008 move from PASIS (3 years' residence) to the PBS (20 years). It lengthened the waiting period without changing the answer option. Ley 18.156 is an optional exemption for foreign technicians covered abroad and does not deny anyone access. No court ruling was relied on.

answers_by_date.answer: Yes, immediate equal access to all types of unemployment benefits
answers_by_date.basis: Before the unemployment-insurance law, the only scheme was the cesantía subsidy in DFL 150 (1981/82), Title II, arts. 41 ff. Art. 43 grants it to dependent workers dismissed for reasons beyond their control who have 12 months of contributions in the previous 2 years. It sets no nationality or residence condition. No practice evidence for this period.

answers_by_date.answer: Yes, immediate equal access to all types of unemployment benefits
answers_by_date.basis: Ley 19.728 (published 2001-05-14; the insurance began operating on 2002-10-01). Art. 1 covers all dependent workers under the Código del Trabajo. Art. 2 excludes only domestic workers, apprentices, under-18s and pensioners, and none of these exclusions turns on nationality. The DFL 150 subsidy remained for workers not covered by the insurance. No practice evidence for this period.

answers_by_date.answer: Yes, immediate equal access to all types of unemployment benefits
answers_by_date.basis: Ley 19.728 was amended (e.g. Ley 20.328, 2009) without any nationality condition. Superintendencia data that combine AFP and unemployment-insurance records show foreign workers affiliated in rising numbers from 2009.

answers_by_date.answer: Yes, immediate equal access to all types of unemployment benefits
answers_by_date.basis: Same provisions. The Labour Directorate's Ord. 1539/17 (2012) confirms that foreign workers, including technicians exempt under Ley 18.156, must contribute to the unemployment insurance, and that it enforces contributions even for workers without a work visa.

answers.sourcing_note: I read the original 2001 text of Ley 19.728 (Justia copy of the LeyChile version) and the current text of DFL 150 art. 43 (SUSESO). LeyChile version histories could not be loaded, so amendments after 2002 (Ley 20.328, 2009; Ley 20.829, 2015) were not read. No practice evidence before 2009.
answers.starting_answer_concern: For 2020 the answer rests on Ley 19.728 art. 1, not on Ley 21.325 arts. 13–14 (in force 2022). 'Effectively Always' overlooks informality and RUN delays among migrants; 'Usually' would be more defensible. Domestic workers were excluded until Ley 21.269 (2020), but that exclusion applied to nationals too.
answers.notes: No nationality condition at any date. In 2000 the only scheme was the DFL 150 subsidy; from October 2002 the Ley 19.728 insurance applied. Both were open to foreign dependent workers on the same terms as nationals.
